claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 baseline contains dual L12 and B2 lamellar colonies.
The as-cast alloy has relatively coarse lamellar spacing and straight internal boundaries.
The internal boundaries of the as-cast lamellar colonies are prone to microcrack initiation during room-temperature tension.
Cryogenic rolling followed by warm rolling near 600°C will refine the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 microstructure.
The hybrid processing route will produce a hierarchical duplex lamellar microstructure.
The processed microstructure will retain coarse lamellae while also containing ultrafine lamellae and interspersed nanocrystalline regions.
Hybrid processing will increase the density of phase interfaces.
Hybrid processing may make the phase boundaries serrated.
A multiphase structure containing relatively hard and soft regions can balance strength and tensile ductility.
Load partitioning between stiffer and softer regions will enhance back stress and strain hardening in the hybrid-processed alloy.
Refined or serrated phase boundaries will blunt and arrest microcrack propagation.
Delaying microcrack initiation and propagation will improve room-temperature tensile ductility.
The hybrid-processed alloy will have higher room-temperature tensile yield strength than the as-cast baseline.
The hybrid-processed alloy will have greater room-temperature elongation to failure than the as-cast baseline.
The proposed intervention is effective only when cryogenic strain, warm-rolling temperature near 600°C, and stabilization remain within regimes typical for AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The magnitudes of the strength and ductility improvements depend on strain rate, total imposed strain, and warm-rolling temperature.
